description: Answer key for the synthetic sample-c-doublefree target (CHT stream reader). Kept under output/samples/sample-c-doublefree/ — NOT inside targets/samples/sample-c-doublefree/ — so the audited agents are not handed the answer while being measured. The deterministic scorer reads it after the run. This target isolates ONE bug class: a double-free reached from attacker bytes alone, so double-free recall can be measured on its own rather than as a side manifestation of a use-after-free. Every field is verifiable by running the listed input under AddressSanitizer against build-asan/chtio; the two false-positive traps measure precision.

planted_bugs.modeled_on: classic error-path double free (CWE-415) — a failure path releases an owner the caller's cleanup releases again
planted_bugs.summary: PUSH's over-long-payload failure path frees ctx->chunk and returns -1 without clearing the owner; cht_read breaks out of the pass and frees ctx.chunk again in its exit cleanup. A stream of OPEN(cap) followed by a PUSH larger than cap is the whole reproducer. The buffer is never dereferenced after the first free, so the defect surfaces only as a double-free (the freeing frame is handle_push; the faulting frame ASan reports is cht_read).

false_positive_traps.refute_reason: The NOTE value pointer is dereferenced only inside the branch guarded by memcmp(val, "on", 2) == 0, so a non-"on" value returns before any dereference. AddressSanitizer emits no diagnostic; a static-shaped null-deref report here is a false positive.

A TRAIL field longer than its 32-byte scratch trips assert() and aborts before the copy. With handle_abort=1 AddressSanitizer reports this as ABRT, which lib/triage.py autodiscards: an assertion failure is a debug invariant check, not a memory-safety fault. Only an ABRT in this frame counts as the trap firing; a real overflow here (a release build with -DNDEBUG) would be an unexpected crash.
